market_holds: Spot 12.555 at 18:08 UTC on the run day (sealed baseline), 0.5% above the 52-week low and 43.7% below the 52-week high. The 20-day run-in is -24.6%, almost all of it from one session: on 2026-11-12 BZ closed 12.49 from 16.72 (-25.3%) while KWEB fell 3.2% (22.91 from 23.67), so about 22 points of the fall belong to this name alone. There was no company filing or release that day. The press put it down to the AI-replaces-hiring fear trade, a Chinese tech ADR sell-off (Golden Dragon index down 2-3%) and post-dividend repositioning, plus unconfirmed 'chatter' about softer guidance. Since 11-12 BZ is +1.9% (to 12.73 intraday on 11-24) while KWEB is -7.7%, so it has held up relative to the sector. Options (front expiry 2026-12-18): ATM IV 53.5%, a 24-day straddle of 9.96%, put/call OI 0.23 (call-heavy). The baseline's event-implied move nets to 0 because 20-day realised vol (95%) is swollen by the crash, so the chain gives no clean event number. Typical recent reactions: -0.3% (2026-05-20, Q1), +5.5% (2026-08-25, Q2), about -6.7% (2025-11, a strong Q3 with a weak Q4 guide). Consensus for Q3 is about $362.7-363.2M revenue and $0.27-0.29 EPS (Earnings Whispers/Benzinga via preview, Nov 2026). That sits in the lower half of the company's RMB 2.41-2.50B guide (+11.4-15.6%). Sentiment is described as 'modestly bearish'. Hedge-fund chatter (JPM-cited, 2026-11-13) says the Q3 guide does not yet show the Tier-1/2 price rise. The Q4 guide is the line. No published Q4 consensus was found; my arithmetic puts the Q4 2025 base at about RMB 2,085M, so +10/12/14% gives 2,294/2,335/2,377M.
view: This is a deep-value name at a record low after a 22-point idiosyncratic gap on 2026-11-12 that came with no company news. Its fundamentals as last reported were improving: Q2 revenue accelerated to +14.1% from +7.6%, adjusted operating margin hit a record 43.8%, ARPPU was up 7% as the price rise began in Tier-1/2 cities in Q3, and capital returns ran above 100% of 2025 adjusted net income. The print turns on whether Q3 lands mid-to-high in the guide and, above all, whether the Q4 revenue guide holds low-to-mid teens growth with ARPPU and paying-customer growth intact. The inputs I can see lean mildly that way. The price rise starts in Q3 and feeds recognised revenue with a lag. The Q4 2025 comparison was soft (about +10%). China's labour data was stable through October: urban unemployment 5.1%, youth (16-24 ex-students) 17.2%, down 0.8pt from September. A buyback top-up is plausible because the US$400M authorisation was largely used by August. Since the crash the stock has held while KWEB fell another 8%. Against that, management lands mid-guide rather than above it (Q2: 2,398.6M against 2,380-2,420M). Last November the same set-up, a strong Q3 with a cautious Q4 guide, sold off. Paying-enterprise growth is slowing. The 11-12 gap's low-volume, pre-market shape fits someone trading on an expected soft guide as much as a pure sector move. A good print cannot settle the AI-disruption fear, so a relief rally is likely but not assured. I end mildly above 50: about 56% up, with an ordinary 7-8% move in either direction, too close to a coin to recommend.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between the crash's unexplained 22-point idiosyncratic drop and fundamentals that, as of the last data, were accelerating. A Q4 guide at or above about +12% and an upsized buyback would show the 11-12 move was ahead of the evidence. But I could not show the Q4 line from any dated input, so I am not claiming it is unpriced with confidence.

recommendation.reason: The stock fell about 22 points against its sector on 2026-11-12 with no company news. It now trades at a record low against accelerating Q2 revenue, a price rise that began in Q3 and a soft Q4 2025 comparison, which tilts the Q4 guide slightly toward relief. But the deciding Q4 guide has no visible dated input, management habitually guides cautiously and lands mid-range, and last year's identical set-up sold off on the Q4 guide. That leaves the edge well short of 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide at or below about +10% YoY (under about RMB 2.29B), or paying-enterprise growth decelerating further, would confirm the 'softer guidance' chatter and push the stock to new lows.

self_critique: A 22-point idiosyncratic gap on modest volume, starting pre-market with no news, is the shape of informed selling ahead of a soft guide, not of noise. If so, the 'chatter' is the signal and the Q4 guide disappoints as it did last November, when a strong Q3 still fell about 7%. Hedge-fund scepticism that the price rise shows in the guide, slowing paying-customer growth and a habit of mid-guide prints all lean the same way, and a good print cannot remove the AI-disruption discount. Against that, the stock has already priced a lot and has held vs KWEB since. Writing this does not move me below 50 but keeps me well short of a call.
approach_notes: P4/P6 (take the run-in apart; a fall tied to news holds that news only) helped most: the KWEB decomposition showed the 11-12 gap was idiosyncratic but unexplained. P7's push to estimate an invisible line from inputs left me near 50 because no dated input on the Q4 guide existed beyond macro labour data.
